🇬🇧 You genuinely could not make this up.

In June, John Healey resigned as Defence Secretary. His words: the Treasury "has been unwilling to commit the resources that the nation needs to defend the country," and he was being forced into decisions that "could make the country less safe." The military asked for ~£28bn; it was offered ~£13.5bn. He walked on principle.

Five weeks later, Andy Burnham made him CHANCELLOR — head of the very Treasury he'd just blamed.

So the excuse is gone. He can't point down the corridor any more. HE holds the purse strings now. The block he resigned over is his own office.

So where's the money, John? If £28bn was essential to keep us safe in June, the Chancellor who said so can commit it today. Nothing is stopping him. Instead his opening moves were a VAT cut and scrapping digital ID — not the rearmament he called a matter of national safety.

Either the money he called essential appears — or the resignation was never principle, just positioning.

Reform UK would fund our Armed Forces to meet the threats we actually face. Defence is the first duty of government, not a bargaining chip. Go figure.
